Rashi on Pesachim 35a:11:2.hebrew: חייבת בחלה - דמין דגן הוי. ואע"ג דחלת לחם כתיב בה, וגמר לחם לחם מלחם עוני במנחות בפרק ר' ישמעאל (מנחות דף ע:) — אורז נמי לחם הוא:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:11:2.english: [Is] obligated in ḥalla - For it is a species of grain. And even though "ḥalla of bread" is written regarding it, and [the Gemara] derives [by verbal analogy] "bread," "bread," from "bread of affliction" in Menachot in the chapter [entitled] Rabbi Yishmael (Menachot 70b) — [according to Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri,] rice too is bread.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:11:3.hebrew: שיצניתא - קצח, שקורין נייל"א בלע"ז. עגול הוא כעין דוחן, ושחור. לישנא אחרינא שמעתי: אשדרניל"א, ונמצאת בשיפון:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:11:3.english: Shitzanita - Ketzaḥ [black cumin], which is called nielle in Old French. It is round like millet, and black. Another version I heard: Esdarnelle [darnel], and it is found in rye.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:11:4.hebrew: כלניתא - מק' (מ"ק: פרג) בלע"ז:

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:12:1.english: With wine and with oil - That one did not put water into it.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:12:2.hebrew: אין חייבין על חימוצו כרת - דמי פירות אין מחמיצין, כדלקמן:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:12:2.english: One is not liable to karet for its leavening - For fruit juices do not cause leavening, as [explained] below.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:13:1.english: Rich matza - And the Merciful One said: “Bread of affliction” (Deuteronomy 16:3).

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:14:1.hebrew: המחהו וגמעו - אשום לחם דמין דגן קאי, ואשמעינן דגמיעה כאכילה לחייבו:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:14:1.english: [If] he dissolved it and swallowed it - It refers to the designation of bread made of a species of grain, and it teaches us that swallowing is [treated] like eating to render him liable.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:14:2.hebrew: המחה - דישטנפרי"ר בלע"ז, שהמחהו במים:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:14:2.english: Dissolved [it] - Destemprer in Old French, [meaning] that he dissolved it in water.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:14:3.english: A person does not fulfill his obligation with it - For he is not eating it in the [normal] manner of eating.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:1:1.hebrew: אלא מעלה - בעלמא הוא מדרבנן, שתהא חיותן בכלי, ואסמכוה רבנן אקרא:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:1:1.english: Rather, [it is] a higher standard - It is merely rabbinic [law] that their freshness must be in the vessel, and the Sages supported it with a verse.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:1:2.hebrew: הכא נמי מעלה - בעלמא הוא, דאין זריעה לתרומה, ואסורין מלאכול:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:1:2.english: Here too, [it is] a higher standard - It is merely [a higher standard] that there is no [purification through] planting for teruma, and [therefore] they are forbidden to be eaten.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:2:1.english: We learned - That the Sages established a higher standard for consecrated items, even [where one is pure] by Torah law.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:2:2.hebrew: בקדשים לא - אם טומאה דבת כפרה היא, כגון זב וזבה ויולדת:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:2:2.english: With regard to consecrated food, no - [This applies] if it is an impurity that requires atonement, such as a zav, a zavah, and a woman who gave birth.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:3:1.hebrew: והבשר - "כל טהור יאכל וגו'". וי"ו יתירה לרבות עצים ולבונה של קודש לטומאה, וקאי אדלעיל: "והבשר אשר יגע בכל טמא לא יאכל" — והבשר:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:3:1.english: And the flesh - [In the clause,] “anyone who is pure may eat...” etc., [there is] a superfluous [letter] vav to include consecrated wood and frankincense regarding ritual impurity. And it refers back to that which is [stated] above: “And the flesh that touches any ritually impure thing shall not be eaten” — “and the flesh.”

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:3:2.hebrew: איטמויי נינהו - בתמיה: הא לאו אוכל נינהו?! מתני' - אלו דברים שאדם יוצא בהן ידי חובתו: משום חובת מצה בלילה ראשונה, שהוא מחוייב לאכול מצה, כדכתיב (שמות י״ב:י״ח) "בערב תאכלו מצות":
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:3:2.english: Are they [capable of] becoming ritually impure - [This is asked] in astonishment: Are they not non-food?! [Mishnah:] "These are the matters with which a person fulfills his obligation" — regarding the obligation of matza on the first night, when he is obligated to eat matza, as it is written (Exodus 12:18): "In the evening you shall eat matzot."

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:4:1.hebrew: אלו דברים שאדם יוצא בהן ידי חובתו - משום חובת מצה בלילה ראשונה, שהוא מחוייב לאכול מצה, כדכתיב (שמות י״ב:י״ח): ״בערב תאכלו מצות״:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:4:1.english: These are the things with which a person fulfills his obligation - [This is] on account of the obligation of matza on the first night, as one is obligated to eat matza, as it is written (Exodus 12:18): "In the evening you shall eat matzot."

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:4:3.hebrew: שיבולת שועל - אביינ"א (שיבולת שועל), שיבולת שלה עשוי כזנב שועל:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:4:3.english: Oats [shibbolet shu’al] - Aveine [oats]. (Shibbolet shu’al:) Its ear is shaped like a fox’s tail.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:4:4.hebrew: יוצאין בדמאי - תבואה הנלקחת מעם הארץ, והיא נקראת דמאי — ספק עישרה, ספק לא עישרה — וחייבו חכמים להפריש מעשרותיה מספק. ואם אכל מצה ממנה ולא הפריש מעשר ממנה — יצא:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:4:4.english: One fulfills [his obligation] with demai - Produce that is purchased from an am ha’aretz, and it is called demai — [as it is] uncertain whether he tithed it [or] uncertain whether he did not tithe it — and the Sages obligated [one] to separate its tithes out of doubt. And if he ate matza from it and did not separate tithe from it, he has fulfilled [his obligation].

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:4:5.english: And with first tithe - [Which belongs] to the Levites.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:4:6.hebrew: שנטלה תרומתו - תרומת מעשר לכהן, ומכאן ואילך המעשר מותר לזרים:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:4:6.english: From which its teruma was taken - [Namely,] the terumat ma’aser [given] to the priest; and from this point onward, the tithe is permitted to non-priests.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:4:7.hebrew: והכהנים בחלה ובתרומה - אבל ישראל בתרומה — לא, כדיליף לקמן: "לא תאכל עליו חמץ שבעת ימים תאכל עליו מצות" — מי שאינו מוזהר על חימוצו אלא משום חמץ, אתה יוצא בו ידי חובת מצה; יצא זה, שאסור מחמת איסור אחר:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:4:7.english: And the priests with ḥalla and with teruma - But an Israelite [does] not [fulfill his obligation] with teruma, as [the Gemara] derives below: “You shall eat no leavened bread with it; seven days you shall eat unleavened bread with it” — [with that food regarding] which one is not cautioned against its leavening except on account of [the prohibition of] leaven, you fulfill your obligation of matza; this excludes this [produce], which is forbidden on account of another prohibition.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:5:1.english: Nor with second tithe - [This applies] outside of Jerusalem.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:5:2.english: [If] he prepared them for himself - [As] bread of a thanks-offering and [of a] nazirite.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:5:3.hebrew: אין יוצא בהן - ואפילו לא שחט הזבח עליהן, ולא קרא שם עליהן, אלא שעשאן לדעת כן. וטעמא מפרש בגמ':
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:5:3.english: He does not fulfill [his obligation] with them - And [this applies] even if he did not slaughter the sacrifice over them and did not designate a name upon them [as consecrated], but merely made them with that intention. And the reason is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:5:4.hebrew: למכור בשוק - לצורכי לחמי תודה ונזירות: יוצא בהן אם לא מכר להן. וטעמא מפרש בגמרא:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:5:4.english: To sell in the market - [He prepared them] for those in need of loaves of a thanks-offering and naziriteship; he fulfills [the obligation] with them if he did not sell [them] to them. And the reason is explained in the Gemara.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:6:1.hebrew: מין חיטין - לענין תרומה, דאין תורמין ממין על שאינו מינו, ותורמין חיטין על כוסמין:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:6:1.english: A type of wheat - In regard to terumah, as one may not separate terumah from [one] species for that which is not its species, and [therefore] one may separate terumah from wheat for spelt.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:6:4.hebrew: שבילי תעלא - אביינ"א (שיבולת-שועל). תעלא — תרגום של שועל:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:6:4.english: Shevilei ta’ala - Aveine [oats] (shibbolet shu’al). Ta’ala is the [Aramaic] translation of shu’al [fox].

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:7:1.hebrew: דברים הבאין לידי חימוץ אדם יוצא בהן - משום מצה, אם עשאן מצה:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:7:1.english: Substances that come to leavening, a person fulfills [his obligation] with them - As matzah, if he prepared them as matzah.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:8:1.hebrew: אורז ודוחן - אין עושין חמץ, ואם מחמיצין אותן, מסריחין:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:8:1.english: Rice and millet - They do not become leaven, and if one [attempts to] leaven them, they spoil.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:8:2.hebrew: אוסר באורז ודוחן - לאכול הימנו תבשיל בפסח. יש מפרשים: למנחות, משום דכל המנחות באות מצה. ושיבוש הוא, דאין מנחה באה אלא חטים, דכתיב (שמות כ״ט:ב׳): "סולת חטים תעשה אותם", חוץ ממנחת העומר, שאינה באה אלא שעורין, [וכן] מנחת סוטה. ופשיטא דדוחן לא! ומאן פליג עליה דרבי יוחנן בהא, ומי מתיר:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:8:2.english: Prohibits rice and millet - To eat a cooked dish of them on Passover. Some explain: For meal-offerings, because all meal-offerings come [as] matzah. And this is an error, for no meal-offering comes from anything other than wheat, as it is written (Exodus 29:2): "Of fine wheat flour shall you make them" — except for the Omer meal-offering, which comes only [from] barley, [and likewise] the meal-offering of a sotah. And it is obvious that millet [may] not [be used]! And who disagrees with Rabbi Yoḥanan in this [regard], and who permits [it]?

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:9:1.hebrew: שקרוב לחימוץ - אלמא בא לידי חימוץ, ולדידיה יוצאין בו משום מצה:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:9:1.english: That it is close to leavening - Evidently, it comes to [a state of] leavening, and according to him, one fulfills [the obligation of] matzah with it.

Rashi on Pesachim 35a:9:2.hebrew: חמץ גמור לא הוי - ונפקא מינה, דאין ענוש כרת, ואם אכלו בשוגג — אין מביא קרבן:
Rashi on Pesachim 35a:9:2.english: It is not full-fledged leavened bread - And the practical difference [is] that one is not punished with karet, and if he ate it unwittingly, he does not bring a [sin] offering.

Tosafot on Pesachim 35a:6:1.hebrew: כוסמין מין חיטין שיבולת שועל ושיפון מין שעורין - רש"י פירש: לענין דאין תורמין ממין על שאין מינו. ור"י אומר, דבמנחות בפרק ר' ישמעאל (מנחות דף ע.) מוכח בהדיא דברייתא לענין חלה מיתני'. יש מקשין: דתנן במסכת חלה (פ"ד מ"ב): "החיטה אינה מצטרפת עם הכל חוץ מן הכוסמין, והשעורין מצטרפין עם הכל חוץ מן החיטין", אלמא כוסמין בהדי שעורין שפיר דמי! ואומר ר"י, ד"כוסמין מין חיטין" — כלומר: אף מין חיטין, וכל שכן מין שעורין; "שיבולת שועל ושיפון מין שעורין" — ולא מין חטין. והא דתניא התם בריש המסכת: "חמשה דברים חייבין בחלה: החיטין, והשעורין, והכוסמין, ושיבולת שועל, ושיפון — הרי אלו חייבין בחלה, ומצטרפין זה עם זה" — אומר ר"י, דמשני בירושלמי: כאן בנשוך, וכאן בבלול. פי': בנשוך — שכל אחת ואחת נעשה עיסה בפני עצמה, ואחר כן נשכו ונתחברו יחד, התם ודאי אין מצטרפין כולם, אלא כמו שמפורשין; בבלול — שכל הקמחים נילושים יחד ועשו מהן עיסה, בההיא כולם מצטרפים, דחשבינן כולם כאחד:
Tosafot on Pesachim 35a:6:1.english: Spelt is a type of wheat; oats and rye are a type of barley - Rashi explained [that this was taught] regarding [the rule] that one does not separate terumah from [one] species for that which is not its species [and wheat and spelt are considered the same species]. And the Ri says that in Menachot, in the chapter [entitled] "Rabbi Yishmael" (Menachot 70a), it is explicitly proven that the baraita was taught regarding challah. Some raise a difficulty: For we learned in a mishna in Tractate Challah (4:2): "Wheat does not combine with anything except for spelt, and barley combines with everything except for wheat." Evidently, spelt together with barley is fine [i.e., they do combine]! And the Ri says that "spelt is a type of wheat" means: [it is] even a type of wheat, and all the more so a type of barley; [whereas] "oats and rye are a type of barley" — and not a type of wheat. And as for that which is taught there at the beginning of the tractate: "Five things are obligated in challah: wheat, barley, spelt, oats, and rye — these are obligated in challah and combine with one another" — the Ri says that [the Gemara] in the Yerushalmi resolves [this]: Here [it is dealing with dough that is] adhered [nashukh], and here [it is dealing with flour that is] mixed [balul]. Explanation: In [the case of] adhered [dough], where each and every [species] was made into a dough on its own, and afterward they adhered to one another and joined together — there, certainly, not all of them combine, but rather only as is specified [in chapter 4]; in [the case of] mixed [dough], where all the flours were kneaded together and they made a dough from them — in that [case], they all combine, for we consider all of them as one.
